The questions that are not on the quiz yet, grouped by deck. The correct answer is listed after each question. Pick the ones you want to add.

## GitHub Basics (Questions 1-7)

**1.** Who can own a repository?

A) Only an organization
B) Only a collaborator
C) A user or an organization account
D) Only someone with a private repository

**Answer: C**

**2.** Which use is best suited to a private repository?

A) Homework, drafts, and work in progress
B) An open source project
C) A portfolio you want anyone to find
D) Free web hosting for a class demo

**Answer: A**

**3.** Which option should you select when creating a repository so that it starts with a `README.md` file?

A) Add file
B) Create branch
C) Add a README file
D) Add people

**Answer: C**

**4.** A brand new repository with a README starts on which branch?

A) readme
B) main
C) first
D) index

**Answer: B**

**5.** Which icon do you click to edit an existing file such as `README.md`?

A) Gear icon
B) Magnifying glass icon
C) Pencil icon
D) Green Code button

**Answer: C**

**6.** How do you see all the commits in the entire repository?

A) Click History on the far right above a file
B) Open the Actions tab
C) Open Settings
D) Click the Commits label above the list of files on the Code page

**Answer: D**

**7.** How do you see only the commits that changed `README.md`?

A) Open the file and click History
B) Click the Commits label on the Code page
C) Open Settings and select Collaborators
D) Click the pencil icon

**Answer: A**

## GitHub Pages (Questions 8-12)

**8.** What is the address format of a GitHub Pages website?

A) `github.com/pages/username`
B) `username.com/repository-name`
C) `repository-name.github.com/username`
D) `username.github.io/repository-name`

**Answer: D**

**9.** To publish from the `main` branch, what do you choose under Build and deployment?

A) Deploy from a branch, then select the `main` branch and the `/ (root)` folder
B) Deploy from a codespace, then select a collaborator
C) Merge from a branch, then select Private
D) Create a repository, then select Add a README file

**Answer: A**

**10.** Where do you watch the progress of a GitHub Pages deployment?

A) Settings, then Collaborators
B) The Commits label
C) The branch menu
D) The Actions tab

**Answer: D**

**11.** In the Actions tab, what does a yellow circle mean?

A) The deployment failed
B) The deployment is still running
C) The deployment is complete
D) The website was deleted

**Answer: B**

**12.** How do you add the website link to the repository's main page?

A) Rename the repository
B) Merge a branch into `main`
C) Select the gear icon next to About and enter the address in the Website field
D) Create a new branch called website

**Answer: C**

## GitHub Codespaces (Questions 13-16)

**13.** When you commit changes in a codespace, where do they go?

A) To `main` automatically
B) To a new repository
C) Nowhere
D) Back to the same branch the codespace was created from

**Answer: D**

**14.** How do you create a codespace on a branch?

A) Open Settings and select Codespaces
B) Select the branch, click the green Code button, open the Codespaces tab, and click Create codespace
C) Open the Actions tab and select New
D) Click the pencil icon on the branch

**Answer: B**

**15.** Which editor runs inside a codespace?

A) Visual Studio Code
B) Notepad
C) Microsoft Word
D) Xcode

**Answer: A**

**16.** Which is a reason to use a codespace instead of the pencil icon on GitHub?

A) It hides your files from collaborators
B) It makes the repository public
C) It makes editing many files, and creating folders, easier
D) It merges branches automatically

**Answer: C**

## The Command Line (Questions 17-19)

**17.** What is the command line?

A) A way to control the computer by typing commands and pressing Enter
B) A line of buttons at the top of a website
C) A way to control the computer only by clicking
D) A list of the files in a repository

**Answer: A**

**18.** What is the difference between the terminal and the shell?

A) The terminal reads your commands and the shell is the window
B) The terminal is the window where you type, and the shell is the program that reads and runs your commands
C) They are the same thing
D) The shell is a website and the terminal is a repository

**Answer: B**

**19.** What is Bash?

A) A branch in a repository
B) A website hosting service
C) A text editor
D) A shell that is the default on Linux and in GitHub Codespaces

**Answer: D**

## Vibe Coding (Questions 20-24)

**20.** What is FigmaMake?

A) A shell like Bash
B) A vibe coding tool for design prototyping within Figma
C) A database on DoltHub
D) A branch of a repository

**Answer: B**

**21.** Which of these is typically NOT included when vibe coding?

A) Writing a prompt
B) Designing the user interface
C) Version tracking
D) Generating a prototype

**Answer: C**

**22.** Which item that vibe coding usually leaves out is source control that manages code changes over time?

A) Authentication
B) Version tracking
C) Database
D) Publishing

**Answer: B**

**23.** What is a Plan document?

A) A short spec of what the app should do, written before you start vibe coding
B) A list of the commits in a repository
C) A branch that holds the plan
D) A page published with GitHub Pages

**Answer: A**

**24.** In the counter web app plan, by which amounts can the counter be incremented or decremented?

A) 1, 3, 5, and 10
B) 1, 2, 10, and 100
C) 1, 2, 5, and 10
D) Only by 1

**Answer: C**

## Large Language Models (Question 25)

**25.** How do you prompt an LLM with both video and audio?

A) Open a repository on GitHub
B) Use a terminal
C) Use a keyboard only
D) Use a webcam, speaking and showing the model what you want

**Answer: D**

## A Modern AI Application (Questions 26-30)

**26.** How is the original (non-AI) FIT Retail Index hosted?

A) On a traditional paid server
B) Free on GitHub, with no traditional server
C) Inside a codespace
D) On DoltHub

**Answer: B**

**27.** Where does the FIT Retail Index get its financial data?

A) From values typed into `index.html`
B) From the README
C) From a codespace
D) From a DoltHub database, through a REST API

**Answer: D**

**28.** What does the original FIT Retail Index let you do?

A) Compare one company against another, or against the segment it belongs to
B) Chat with an AI
C) Write Markdown
D) Create branches

**Answer: A**

**29.** What is new in the AI version of the FIT Retail Index?

A) It is hosted on GitHub
B) It uses financial data for retail companies
C) It has LLM Chat that can query the same DoltHub database
D) It has no database

**Answer: C**

**30.** In the AI version, what can the AI do with the menus on the company to company page?

A) Delete them
B) See their state and set them for you
C) Rename them
D) Publish them

**Answer: B**

## Strudel (Questions 31-32)

**31.** What is Strudel?

A) A version tracking tool
B) A shell for typing commands
C) A hosting service for websites
D) A musical language for live coding and DJing

**Answer: D**

**32.** Strudel is based on Tidal Cycles. Which programming language is Tidal Cycles written in?

A) Haskell
B) Python
C) Bash
D) Markdown

**Answer: A**

## Assignments (Questions 33-39)

**33.** In the Hw GitHub Basics assignment, what repository do you create?

A) `my-simple-webpage`, private
B) `my-simple-webpage`, public
C) `README`, public
D) `index.html`, private

**Answer: B**

**34.** Which items must the `README.md` include in the assignment?

A) A table, an image, a link, and a heading
B) Only a heading
C) A bullet list, a numbered list, italic text, and bold text
D) Only a bullet list

**Answer: C**

**35.** Where do you commit your changes in the assignment?

A) On a new branch
B) In a codespace
C) In a terminal
D) Directly to `main`

**Answer: D**

**36.** How do you upload `index.html` to your repository?

A) Select Add file, then Upload files
B) Open Settings, then Collaborators
C) Open the Actions tab
D) Copy it into `README.md`

**Answer: A**

**37.** In the Stitch ordering spec, what kind of app must you create?

A) A Mobile App
B) A WebApp
C) A terminal app
D) A command line tool

**Answer: B**

**38.** What prominent element must Page 2, Ready to Pay, include?

A) A logo carousel
B) A branch menu
C) A Submit Order button
D) A Delete button

**Answer: C**

**39.** What does the Stitch ordering spec say about the menu?

A) You may rename the items
B) You may change the prices
C) You may add new items
D) Use the menu exactly, with no added, removed, or renamed items and no changed prices

**Answer: D**

## More Questions (Questions 40-48)

**40.** How do you create a new file in a repository on GitHub?

A) Click the pencil icon on `README.md`
B) Open Settings and select New file
C) Click the Commits label
D) Select Add file, then Create new file

**Answer: D**

**41.** How do you delete a file from a repository on GitHub?

A) Open the file, open its menu, select Delete file, and commit the change
B) Click the gear icon next to About
C) Open the branch menu and select Delete
D) Open the Actions tab and select the file

**Answer: A**

**42.** Before you create a new branch in a new repository, what does the branch menu say?

A) origin
B) main
C) branch
D) root

**Answer: B**

**43.** Which kinds of files can a GitHub Pages website use?

A) Only Markdown files
B) Only images
C) Only Word documents
D) HTML, CSS, and JavaScript files

**Answer: D**

**44.** In the Actions tab, what does a green check mark mean for a deployment?

A) The deployment is still running
B) The deployment failed
C) The deployment is complete
D) The website was deleted

**Answer: C**

**45.** What is true about the first time a codespace starts?

A) It is faster than later starts
B) It takes longer than later starts
C) It deletes the repository
D) It only works on `main`

**Answer: B**

**46.** What does GitHub do while a codespace starts?

A) Deletes the branch
B) Emails your collaborators
C) Publishes the repository as a website
D) Builds the machine and copies the repository onto it

**Answer: D**

**47.** In the counter web app plan, what does the reset button do?

A) Doubles the counter
B) Deletes the app
C) Sets the counter back to 0
D) Changes the amount to 10

**Answer: C**

**48.** Which is an example of a financial data source an LLM can use as a tool?

A) A README file
B) A branch
C) Yahoo Finance
D) A commit message

**Answer: C**
